name: MarqueeFlow
author: tupacan

sections.description:
MarqueeFlow turns images from your WordPress Media Library into continuously scrolling marquees. Use it for partner logos, brand strips, photography and image showcases — directly in the block editor.

Both logos and photographs work in the free plugin. Choose your images, arrange their order and adjust the Images and Animation settings. No account or license is needed to use Free.

The scrolling animation uses CSS transforms rather than a JavaScript animation library. Visitors who prefer reduced motion see a horizontally scrollable image strip instead of automatic scrolling.

Included in Free

  • Continuously scrolling image strips
  • Slow, Normal and Fast animation presets
  • Small (40px), Medium (60px) and Large (80px) image-height presets
  • Normal and Spacious gap presets
  • Maximum image width settings to keep wide images in proportion
  • Left-to-right or right-to-left movement
  • Optional pause on hover
  • Adjustable image corner radius
  • Live editor preview and drag-and-drop image reordering
  • Wide and full-width block alignment, where supported by your theme
  • Reduced-motion support and image alternative text

Get started

  1. Add the MarqueeFlow block to a page or post in the WordPress block editor.
  2. Select images from your Media Library or upload new ones.
  3. Drag the image thumbnails into the order you want.
  4. Adjust image sizing, spacing and corner radius in Images, and speed, direction and pause on hover in Animation.
  5. Publish or update your page.

For a smooth scrolling strip, start with at least six images. You can add several MarqueeFlow blocks to a page and give each its own settings.

Optional MarqueeFlow Pro add-on

Pro adds more control over the same logo and photo marquees:

  • Custom image height and gap in pixels
  • Faded left and right edges
  • Image opacity
  • Grayscale and inverted grayscale effects

Pro is a separate paid add-on. Keep the free MarqueeFlow plugin installed and active, install the Pro add-on, and activate an eligible license to unlock paid controls and effects.

See MarqueeFlow Pro features and plans.

Free works independently. Removing Pro or losing an eligible license returns paid settings to Free behavior without deleting the saved Pro settings.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins → Add New Plugin and search for MarqueeFlow.
  2. Install and activate MarqueeFlow.
  3. Open a page or post in the block editor and add the MarqueeFlow block.

To install a downloaded ZIP, use Plugins → Add New Plugin → Upload Plugin, choose the ZIP, then install and activate it.
sections.faq:
Can I use photographs, or only logos?

Both. Free supports logo strips and photograph marquees. Pro is needed for custom height and gap values, not for using photographs. The free image-height presets are 40px, 60px and 80px.

Does MarqueeFlow work with the classic editor or other page builders?

MarqueeFlow is a native WordPress block and requires the WordPress block editor. It does not currently provide a shortcode or a dedicated integration for other page builders.

Which image formats can I use?

Use image formats supported by your WordPress installation, such as JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF and AVIF. Format availability can depend on your WordPress version and hosting environment.

WordPress does not permit SVG uploads by default. SVG uploads require a suitable sanitizing plugin, such as Safe SVG. MarqueeFlow does not enable SVG uploads itself.

Does it use JavaScript on the frontend?

MarqueeFlow uses CSS for its frontend scrolling animation and does not enqueue a frontend JavaScript animation script. The block editor uses JavaScript to provide its editing controls. Your theme and other plugins may load their own scripts.

How can I keep the marquee lightweight?

Use appropriately sized, compressed images. CSS animation avoids a frontend animation library, but image size, image count and the rest of your page still affect loading and rendering performance.

What happens when a visitor prefers reduced motion?

When the visitor’s device or browser requests reduced motion, the marquee stops scrolling automatically and the images can be scrolled horizontally instead.

Do I need an account or a license?

No account or license is required for Free. The optional Pro add-on uses Freemius to manage paid licensing and requires an eligible activated license for its paid settings.

What happens if my Pro license expires or I deactivate Pro?

Paid controls and effects stop applying, and the marquee uses Free behavior. This can change its displayed sizing, spacing and effects. Saved Pro settings are retained so they can apply again when Pro is active with an eligible license. Cached pages may need to refresh before the change appears.

Is WordPress Multisite supported?

The initial supported scope is ordinary single-site WordPress installations. Multisite networks have not yet been validated for support.
sections.changelog:
1.0.4

  • Clarified Free and Pro features, setup instructions and licensing information.
  • Refreshed the plugin-directory banner, screenshots and captions.
  • No changes to block controls or frontend behavior.

1.0.3

  • Add a compact Pro plans panel in the block sidebar and a plugin-row pricing link.
  • Hide Free promotion when the separate Pro add-on is active.
  • Keep all Free controls and frontend behavior unchanged.

1.0.2

  • Reorganized block settings into Images and Animation panels.
  • Added an image corner radius control and clearer spacing between settings.

1.0.1

  • Fix full-width layouts inside themes with global padding.
  • Preserve image metadata when editing or reordering media selections.
  • Retain inactive saved settings while rendering supported Free values.
  • Add versioned extension hooks without bundling paid features.
  • Improve duplicate-set link keyboard handling for extensions.
  • Hide Pro promotion until the Pro launch.
  • Compatibility checked with WordPress 7.1.

1.0.0

  • Initial release
  • Marquee animation with three speed presets
  • Image height presets (Small, Medium, Large)
  • Gap presets (Normal, Spacious)
  • Max image width control
  • Direction control (left-to-right, right-to-left)
  • Pause on hover
  • Drag-and-drop image reordering
  • Accessible: ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, reduced motion support
